column9: stem
column28: explanation

column9: The electrons in the outermost energy level of an atom are called…
column28: Valence electrons are the outermost electrons. They are the ones used in bonding.

column9: Atoms bond so that they end up with a full outer energy level.
column28: True. Atoms gain, lose, or share electrons to fill their outer level, which makes them stable.

column9: Chlorine is in group 17. How many valence electrons does a chlorine atom have?
column28: For groups 13–18, drop the 1: group 17 has 7 valence electrons.

column9: Most atoms are stable when their outer energy level holds how many electrons?
column28: A full outer level is 8 electrons (an octet). Helium is the exception with 2.

column9: An atom that LOSES electrons becomes…
column28: Losing negative electrons leaves more protons than electrons, so the ion is positive: a cation.

column9: How many dots go in the electron dot diagram for carbon?
column28: Carbon is in group 14, so it has 4 valence electrons: 4 dots.

column9: Noble gases bond easily with other elements.
column28: False. Noble gases already have a full outer level, so they are stable and rarely bond.

column9: Which element has the same number of valence electrons as oxygen?
column28: Oxygen and sulfur are both in group 16, so each has 6 valence electrons.

column9: What is the oxidation number of chlorine (Cl)? Include the sign. Oxidation number: ___
column28: Chlorine (group 17) has 7 valence electrons and gains 1 to fill its outer level: −1.

column9: What is the oxidation number of calcium (Ca)? Include the sign. Oxidation number: ___
column28: Calcium is in group 2. It loses its 2 valence electrons: +2.

column9: Aluminum is in group 13. How many valence electrons does it have?
column28: For groups 13–18, drop the 1: group 13 has 3 valence electrons.

column9: When they bond with a metal, the elements in group 17 usually…
column28: Group 17 atoms have 7 valence electrons, so gaining 1 is the easiest way to reach 8.

column9: Lithium has 3 electrons in all. Why does its electron dot diagram show only 1 dot?
column14: A dot diagram shows only protons
column15: Two of its electrons were lost
column16: A dot diagram shows only valence electrons, and lithium has 1
column28: Dot diagrams show only the outer (valence) electrons. Lithium is in group 1, so it has 1.

column9: Which group of elements has an oxidation number of +1?
column28: Group 1 atoms have 1 valence electron and lose it, giving a +1 charge.

column9: A sodium ion (Na⁺) has more electrons than protons.
column28: False. Na⁺ has lost an electron, so it has 11 protons and only 10 electrons. That is why it is positive.

column9: Which of these elements LOSE electrons when they form ions? Choose all that apply.
column28: Sodium, calcium, and aluminum are metals with 1, 2, and 3 valence electrons, so they lose them. Chlorine and oxygen are nonmetals that gain electrons.

column9: How many dots go in the electron dot diagram for neon?
column28: Neon is in group 18 with a full outer level of 8 valence electrons: 8 dots.

column9: A chlorine atom gains one electron. Which noble gas does the chloride ion now match?
column28: Chlorine has 17 electrons. Gaining 1 makes 18, the same as argon.

column9: An atom has 6 valence electrons. What charge will its ion most likely have?
column28: Gaining 2 electrons is much easier than losing 6. Two extra electrons give a charge of −2.

column9: Nitrogen is in group 15. What charge does a nitrogen ion have? Include the sign. Charge: ___
column28: Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons and gains 3 to reach 8: −3.

column9: Element X forms an ion with a +2 charge. Which group is X most likely in?
column28: A +2 charge means the atom lost 2 valence electrons. Group 2 elements have 2 valence electrons.

column9: Neon has 10 electrons. Which of these ions also have 10 electrons? Choose all that apply.
column28: Na⁺ is 11 − 1 = 10, F⁻ is 9 + 1 = 10, and Mg²⁺ is 12 − 2 = 10. Cl⁻ and K⁺ each have 18, like argon.

column9: Magnesium has 2 valence electrons. Why does it lose 2 electrons instead of gaining 6?
column14: Magnesium cannot hold more than 2 electrons
column15: Losing 2 takes far less energy than gaining 6, and it leaves a full level underneath
column16: Gaining electrons would make it a different element
column17: Metals have no outer energy level
column28: Atoms take the easier path to a full outer level. Losing 2 electrons uncovers the full level below.

column9: An oxygen atom has 8 protons. How many electrons does an oxide ion (O²⁻) have?
column28: A −2 charge means 2 more electrons than protons: 8 + 2 = 10.

column9: In an ionic bond, electrons are…
column15: transferred from one atom to another
column28: In an ionic bond the metal gives electrons to the nonmetal. The opposite charges then attract.

column9: Ionic bonds usually form between a metal and a nonmetal.
column28: True. The metal loses electrons and the nonmetal gains them.

column9: What is the name of LiF?
column28: Name the metal (lithium), then the nonmetal with an -ide ending (fluoride).

column9: In the name of a two-element ionic compound, the ending of the nonmetal changes to…
column28: Chlorine becomes chloride, oxygen becomes oxide, sulfur becomes sulfide.

column9: What charge does a magnesium ion carry? Include the sign. Charge: ___
column28: Magnesium is in group 2 and loses its 2 valence electrons: +2.

column9: A positively charged ion is called…
column28: Cations are positive (metals form them). Anions are negative.

column9: In the formula for an ionic compound, the nonmetal is written first.
column28: False. The positive ion (the metal) is written first, as in NaCl.

column9: What is the name of CaCl₂?
column28: Ionic names do not use prefixes, and calcium always forms +2, so no Roman numeral: calcium chloride.

column9: What is the formula for magnesium oxide?
column28: Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ cancel one for one: MgO.

column9: What is the formula for sodium sulfide?
column28: Na⁺ is +1 and S²⁻ is −2, so it takes 2 sodium ions for each sulfide ion: Na₂S.

column9: Which formula stands for the sulfate ion?
column28: Sulfate is SO₄²⁻. (OH is hydroxide, PO₄ is phosphate, NH₄ is ammonium.)

column9: What is the charge on the sulfate ion? Include the sign. Charge: ___
column28: Sulfate is SO₄²⁻, so its charge is −2.

column9: In AlCl₃, how many chloride ions are there for each aluminum ion?
column28: The subscript 3 after Cl means 3 chloride ions (−1 each) balance one Al³⁺.

column9: What is the name of K₂O?
column28: Potassium, then oxygen with -ide. No prefixes in ionic names: potassium oxide.

column9: The Roman numeral in iron(II) oxide tells you there are two iron atoms.
column28: False. The Roman numeral gives the charge on the iron ion (+2), not how many atoms there are.

column9: Which pairs of elements would form an IONIC bond? Choose all that apply.
column28: Each of those pairs is a metal with a nonmetal. Carbon and chlorine, and hydrogen and oxygen, are both nonmetals, so they share electrons.

column9: Which polyatomic ion has a POSITIVE charge?
column28: Ammonium is NH₄⁺. The other three are negative.

column9: What is the name of FeCl₃?
column28: Three chloride ions at −1 make −3, so the iron ion is +3: iron(III) chloride.

column9: What is the formula for aluminum oxide?
column28: Al³⁺ and O²⁻: 2 aluminum (+6) balance 3 oxygen (−6). Al₂O₃.

column9: What is the name of Cu₂O?
column28: Oxide is −2. Two copper ions share +2, so each is +1: copper(I) oxide.

column9: What is the formula for calcium nitrate?
column28: Ca²⁺ needs two NO₃⁻ ions. Parentheses show that the whole nitrate ion is doubled: Ca(NO₃)₂.

column9: Which of these names are written correctly? Choose all that apply.
column28: Magnesium always forms +2, so it gets no Roman numeral. The nonmetal needs the -ide ending: sodium chloride, not sodium chlorine.

column9: What is the charge on the lead ion in PbO₂? Include the sign. Charge: ___
column28: Two oxide ions at −2 make −4, so the one lead ion must be +4. The name is lead(IV) oxide.

column9: What is the name of NaOH?
column28: OH is the hydroxide ion. Polyatomic ions keep their own name: sodium hydroxide.

column9: In a covalent bond, electrons are…
column14: transferred from a metal to a nonmetal
column28: Covalent means sharing. Both atoms count the shared electrons toward a full outer level.

column9: Covalent bonds form between nonmetal atoms.
column28: True. Nonmetals both need electrons, so they share instead of transferring.

column9: The prefix "tri" means how many?
column28: Tri means 3, like a tricycle has 3 wheels.

column9: Which prefix means 4?
column28: Tetra = 4. (Tri = 3, penta = 5, hexa = 6.)

column9: What is the name of CO₂?
column28: 1 carbon (no mono on the first element) and 2 oxygen = dioxide.

column9: How many pairs of electrons are shared in a triple bond?
column28: Triple = 3 shared pairs.

column9: The prefix mono- is used on the first element in a covalent name.
column28: False. Mono is left off the first element: CO is carbon monoxide, not monocarbon monoxide.

column9: What is the name of SO₃?
column28: 1 sulfur and 3 oxygen = trioxide.

column9: What is the formula for carbon tetrachloride?
column28: No prefix on carbon means 1. Tetra means 4 chlorine: CCl₄.

column9: What is the name of N₂O₄?
column28: 2 nitrogen = dinitrogen; 4 oxygen = tetroxide.

column9: How many electrons in all are shared in a triple bond?
column28: 3 shared pairs × 2 electrons each = 6 electrons.

column9: What is the formula for dinitrogen pentoxide?
column28: Di = 2 nitrogen; penta = 5 oxygen: N₂O₅.

column9: The prefix "hepta" means how many?
column28: Hepta means 7.

column9: In an H₂ molecule, the two hydrogen atoms…
column15: share 1 pair of electrons, so each has a full first level of 2
column28: Each hydrogen has 1 electron. Sharing the pair gives each atom 2, which fills the first energy level.

column9: A double bond is weaker than a single bond.
column28: False. More shared pairs hold the atoms together more strongly, so a double bond is stronger (and shorter).

column9: Which of these are covalent compounds? Choose all that apply.
column28: CO₂, H₂O, and CH₄ are made only of nonmetals. NaCl and MgO each have a metal, so they are ionic.

column9: What is the name of SF₆?
column28: 1 sulfur and 6 fluorine = hexafluoride.

column9: What is the name of P₂O₅?
column28: 2 phosphorus = diphosphorus; 5 oxygen = pentoxide.

column9: An oxygen atom has 6 valence electrons. What kind of bond joins the two atoms in O₂?
column28: Each oxygen needs 2 more electrons, so the two atoms share 2 pairs: a double bond.

column9: A chlorine atom has 7 valence electrons. In a Cl₂ molecule the two atoms share one pair. How many LONE pairs (pairs that are not shared) are in the whole molecule?
column28: Each chlorine uses 1 electron in the bond and keeps 6, which is 3 lone pairs. 3 + 3 = 6.

column9: Why do covalent names need prefixes?
column15: The same two elements can form more than one compound, such as CO and CO₂
column16: Prefixes show the charge on each ion
column17: Prefixes show which element is heavier
column28: Nonmetals can combine in different ratios, so the name has to say how many atoms of each there are.

column9: Which names match their formulas? Choose all that apply.
column28: SO₂ is sulfur dioxide (no mono on the first element), and PCl₃ is phosphorus trichloride (the second element always gets a prefix).

column9: Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons. It shares electrons with hydrogen atoms until its outer level is full. What is the formula of the molecule?
column28: Nitrogen needs 3 more electrons. Each hydrogen shares 1, so it bonds with 3 hydrogen atoms: NH₃.

column9: What is the name of CS₂?
column28: 1 carbon and 2 sulfur, with the -ide ending = carbon disulfide.

column9: Which type of compound is made of only nonmetals?
column28: Nonmetals share electrons with each other, forming covalent compounds.

column9: Ionic compounds usually have high melting points.
column28: True. The strong attractions between the ions take a lot of energy to break.

column9: Table salt (NaCl) is…
column28: Sodium is a metal and chlorine is a nonmetal, so NaCl is ionic.

column9: One particle of a covalent compound is called…
column28: Atoms that share electrons form a separate particle called a molecule.

column9: Covalent compounds conduct electricity well when they are dissolved in water.
column28: False. Covalent compounds dissolve as neutral molecules, so there are no ions to carry the current.

column9: The ions in a solid ionic compound are packed in a repeating pattern called…
column28: Each ion is held by all of its neighbors in a repeating crystal lattice.

column9: How many oxygen atoms are in one molecule of CO₂?
column28: The subscript 2 after O means 2 oxygen atoms.

column9: Which of these compounds is IONIC?
column28: Potassium is a metal and chlorine is a nonmetal. The other three are made only of nonmetals.

column9: Which of these compounds is COVALENT?
column28: Sulfur and oxygen are both nonmetals. The other three each have a metal.

column9: Sugar dissolves in water, but the solution does not conduct electricity. Sugar is most likely…
column28: No conduction means no ions in the water, which points to a covalent compound.

column9: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?
column14: The attractions between oppositely charged ions are strong and take a lot of energy to break
column17: They are always made of noble gases
column28: Every ion is strongly attracted to its neighbors in the lattice, so it takes a lot of heat to pull them apart.

column9: Which has the HIGHER melting point: NaCl or H₂O?
column15: They melt at the same temperature
column28: Ionic compounds like NaCl melt at much higher temperatures than covalent compounds like water.

column9: What is the TOTAL number of atoms in one molecule of H₂SO₄?
An ionic compound is made of separate molecules.
column28: False. Ionic compounds form one continuous lattice of ions. The formula gives the ratio of ions.

column9: Which properties describe most IONIC compounds? Choose all that apply.
column15: Conduct electricity when dissolved in water
column28: Ionic compounds are hard, brittle crystals with high melting points, and their solutions conduct. Separate molecules made of only nonmetals describes covalent compounds.

column9: Classify CaCl₂.
column17: A mixture of two different substances
column28: Calcium is a metal and chlorine is a nonmetal, so CaCl₂ is an ionic compound.

column9: What carries the electric current in salt water?
column16: Ions that are free to move
column17: Nothing — salt water does not conduct
column28: Dissolved salt breaks into Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions. Moving charged particles carry the current.

column9: A solid melts at 55 °C and does not conduct electricity when dissolved in water. What is it most likely, and why?
column14: Covalent — a low melting point and no ions in the solution
column16: Ionic — a low melting point means strong bonds
column28: A low melting point and a solution that does not conduct both point to a covalent compound.

column9: An unknown substance forms brittle crystals, melts at 770 °C, and conducts electricity when dissolved in water. Which could it be?
column28: Those are ionic properties. KCl is the only choice made of a metal and a nonmetal.

column9: A solid ionic compound does not conduct electricity, but the same compound conducts when it is melted. Why?
column15: When it melts, the ions are free to move
column16: Melting turns it into a covalent compound
column17: Solids have no charges in them
column28: The ions are locked in place in the solid. Once melted they can move and carry a current.

column9: Which of these compounds are IONIC? Choose all that apply.
column28: NaBr, MgO, and K₂S each have a metal and a nonmetal. CO and NH₃ are made only of nonmetals, so they are covalent.

column9: What is the TOTAL number of atoms in Ca(OH)₂? (Watch the parentheses.)
column28: Ca = 1. The 2 doubles everything in the parentheses: O = 2 and H = 2. 1 + 2 + 2 = 5.

column9: A student heats two white solids on a hot plate. Solid A melts in a few seconds. Solid B never melts. Which conclusion fits best?
column14: A is likely ionic and B is likely covalent
column16: A is likely covalent and B is likely ionic
column28: Covalent compounds melt at low temperatures; ionic compounds need far more heat than a hot plate gives.

column9: Which statement is true of BOTH ionic and covalent compounds?
column14: Both are made of two or more elements that are chemically bonded
column28: Any compound is two or more elements bonded together. The other statements fit only one type.
